steps.content: The mechanical rumbling gradually dies down. You lean against the wall, steadying your breath. Norma stands nearby, breathing hard, yet her posture remains perfectly straight. The overhead lights flicker on, and a clinical, high-definition holographic projection slowly appears in the air.

It's Founder "X," the figure that repeatedly appeared in the promotional video. But now, every filter and disguise has been stripped away. The voice and face are no longer obscured. That gentle smile remains, yet it feels unnervingly hollow, like a carefully sculpted mask.
A flicker of icy fury flashes across Norma's eyes.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I was right. It really is you.
The hologram doesn't deny it. Instead, the man surveys the damaged mechanisms around them, as though inspecting the results of a satisfactory experiment.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Did you enjoy yourself, Norma? Quite the thrilling game, wasn't it? And familiar, too, I imagine?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: You plagiarized my model.
The hologram lets out a soft laugh.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Oh, don't say that. This isn't plagiarism. It's refinement. An old prophet like "Moses" no longer fits in the world we live in. What we need is someone brave enough to reshape the future, to rebuild the very logic of our civilization. I've named it "Saint Paul."
He raises one hand, and streams of data unfurl slowly behind him, like a wall woven with countless behavioral patterns.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: What human society truly needs isn't prediction, but control. All the Public Security Bureau can do is mitigate damage after it has been done or issue warnings beforehand. But you can't just calculate or predict chaos away.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Rather than passively waiting for tragedies to happen and then trying to repair the damage, wouldn't it be better to eliminate them at the source?
His voice remains gentle, yet it carries a chilling certainty.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: What I want is a society with real order. No chaos, no accidents, and none of those errors caused by the "complications" of human nature.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Emotions can be guided. Choices can be designed. Behavior can be calculated. When all of this falls under control, order ceases to be a matter of probability. It becomes inevitable. As for democracy, discussion, negotiation between parties... These things sound noble enough, but they're merely noises that slow down the decision-making process.

This seems more like an extremely twisted sense of order than simple lust for power. He genuinely believes that once human emotions, choices, and behavior are brought entirely under control, society will become safer and more stable.
Public security, public opinion, resource allocation, elections... In his eyes, these are all mere parameters that can be rearranged.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: That's why I reversed your model. It's no longer used to predict the future, but to shape it.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...This is your testing ground. Are you using those players as test subjects?

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Test subjects? No.
He shakes his head gently.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Data.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: "Saint Paul" still has its flaws. What I need is authentic human data. I need to understand, under deliberate guidance, how emotions are triggered, how choices are narrowed down, and how conflicts can be led back to the best solution. And the Public Security Bureau cannot provide me with these data.
He turns to look at Norma, undisguised admiration in his gaze.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: You know, Norma, from the very beginning, I saw your model's true potential. That's why I pushed through opposition and brought you into the Public Security Bureau exceptionally. You are the very cornerstone of all of this.
Norma's gaze darkens. All those overlooked details, all those errors she's written off as "coincidence"... At this moment, they piece together a far more cruel and ugly truth.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...Those last-minute adjustments to the patrol rosters, were they really just for accommodating that "inspection"?
The air falls silent for a moment. Then the hologram suddenly begins to clap, laughing cheerfully.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Of course, that was only a pretext, a necessary trigger condition. If I hadn't fabricated an incident "extreme" enough, your model would never have been shut down. And I could never have obtained its source code.

He talks about it so casually. All those bloody deaths, reduced to a single line of negligible footnote. Norma clenches her fists, but quickly regains her composure. Only this time, the coldness in her eyes grows even colder.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Though the current situation is turning out far more interesting than I anticipated.
He leans forward slightly, his tone taking on an edge of inscrutable interest.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: At first, when you volunteered to investigate "Reshaping the Future," it did surprise me a little. I thought you'd already discovered something. I nearly called off this experiment altogether.
He pauses, as if savoring the memory.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: But I quickly realized something. If you could trace your way here, it meant your model must have achieved a new breakthrough. And that was exactly what I needed. You were so insistent, so I thought I would let you into my system. With a few pushes, I might just gain access to your optimized algorithm.

steps.speaker: Herb-Gathering Girl
steps.content: Everything was going so smoothly... until that "anomaly" appeared. Your friend, Eileen.
He says the name in a cold, scrutinizing tone.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Emotional interference, decision deviation, path detachment... She amplified all these negligible noises. And somehow you broke free from the model's constraints because of it. But that only proved one thing: Your value is even greater than I initially calculated.
He extends his hand, his tone composed.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Therefore, instead of continuing to oppose one another, why don't we work together?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...You want me to help you improve "Saint Paul"?

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Exactly. We are indeed quite similar in character, aren't we? We both believe in mathematics and logic, and we despise hypocrisy and chaos. Securing the safety of the majority at a minimal cost—this is the most basic optimization problem.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Once we perfect "Saint Paul," you'll witness firsthand the construction of a society without accidents or casualties.
A faint smile crosses his face as he adds one final point:

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: As for that friend of yours... in a world like that, she would never have to suffer emotional breakdowns or pain again.
A brief silence. Norma lowers her head, her shadow on the floor shifting slightly.
Then...

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: No.
It's one simple word, but it's clear and unwavering, without a trace of hesitation. She lifts her head.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Do you know why I believe in logic? Because logic is part of the world's fundamental truth. It doesn't bend to anyone's will. It doesn't serve anyone's desires. It simply is.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: But everything you just said was based on a single assumption: You think you can define what's "right."
She takes a step forward.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: You start with your desired outcome, then reverse-engineer the process to make it all seem reasonable. But what lies behind it is not reason, but the falsification of logic.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: You disguise control as "safety." You call the stripping of rights "stability." You camouflage the elimination of choice as a "best solution." Then you tell everyone this is right. But you've been constructing a lie from the very beginning.
She pauses for a moment, her voice turning ice cold.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: That incident years ago wasn't a "necessary price." It was the result of your deliberate fabrication. And you didn't build your model to understand the world, but to control it.
Her sharp gaze cuts like a scalpel, methodically peeling away the pretense in his words, laying bare the corruption and self-interest rotting at the core of his so-called logic.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: If conclusions can be bent just to pay a price or serve anyone's interests, then all research will lose its meaning. You've never understood what it means to pursue truth. You just need an excuse that makes you sound reasonable.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: And your so-called "order" is nothing but blasphemy against truth, against science, against logic itself!
Her words resound with firm conviction.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: So don't you dare compare yourself to me. My principles have nothing in common with yours.
The moment she says those words, the hologram's expression freezes completely, then fractures. His calm facade is torn apart, exposing the barely contained rage and bitter indignation beneath.

options: That's enough. End of the debate.

choices.text: That's enough. End of the debate.

steps.content: You step out from the shadows and wave the comms device in your hand before him.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Every word you just said, including the truth about that incident, has already been transmitted to the MBCC in real time.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: What... MBCC... You're...

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: A pleasure to meet you... though I doubt the feeling is mutual. I'm ${PlayerName}, Chief of the MBCC. Everything you just confessed will serve as evidence, and I'll be testifying alongside Norma to ensure you're brought to justice.
The hologram seems taken aback, then laughs abruptly. The single sharp burst of laughter keeps growing louder and more uncontrollable.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: In that case, I have no choice but to eliminate you both!
He raises his hand suddenly. A piercing rumbling erupts as a fresh wave of mechanisms crashes down like a downpour, faster, denser, and more precise than before.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: "Saint Paul" has just digested your behavioral patterns and refined its analysis. This time, there's no chance you're making it out alive!
Just as he says, every move you and Norma make is predicted, disrupting your combat rhythm. The space closes in around you, every inch of your escape route gradually being sealed off.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Watch out!

You turn your head. A spinning metal saw blade is bearing down on you. Time seems to stretch in this instant. You can make out every charred mark left on its surface, see its edges glowing dull red from the friction of its relentless spin.
Too late.

Snap!
The lights go out. Everything grinds to an abrupt halt. The blade stops centimeters from your eye, quivering for a heartbeat before going completely still.
Overhead, the previously steady hologram flickers violently. That "perfect" face begins to distort and warp, as if the signal has been cut off.

Zzzzt.
All of a sudden, the hologram shatters, dissolving into broken flecks of light before vanishing completely. In the brief darkness and silence that follows, you can barely tell where reality ends and illusion begins.

Bang!
Right then, the locked side door is hacked open from the outside! Shattered metal panels crash to the ground as smoke and dust billow through. A figure stands by the door, firefighter ax in hand.

It's Eileen.
Hair utterly disheveled, she's panting, but her eyes are bright with energy.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...Why did you come back?

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: I know what you're about to say. "That's an irrational decision." But if it hadn't been for my "irrationality," you two would have been dead at that scumbag's hands right now!

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I told you to leave. This place is too dangerous for you...

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Oh, just shut up!!
She yells, her sharp and urgent voice ringing through the confined space. A small laugh escapes you. The suffocating tension is torn up instantly by that single shout. You turn to look at Norma.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: "The human heart is an uncontrollable, irrational thing." Isn't that what you always say?

Rendered speechless, Norma simply stares blankly at Eileen like a computer that's just crashed. Eileen, meanwhile, casually raises her hand and dumps the firefighter ax on the ground with a resounding thud.
She looks up toward the concealed door in the distance that was once tightly closed but is now sliding open due to the system failure. Her lips curl into an obvious mocking grin.
Behind it lies a hidden control room. With the power cut, the door unlocks automatically, the heavy panels sliding open inch by inch. The real person standing behind it has nowhere left to hide.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: How can someone be so smart and yet still have never thought of maybe keeping a backup server and power supply?

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: D-d-did you just destroy the server room?

The man stands before the control panel, his face turning deathly pale. Gone is the composure and "perfection" of his projected image. All the control he carefully maintained is completely crushed in this instant. Eileen gives the ax a casual kick, her tone relaxed and scornful.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Took me forever to smash open that fire cabinet and get this ax. Good thing your wiring wasn't that complicated, and I didn't sleep through all my physics classes at school. Found it quickly enough.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Way easier to just cut the power and smash the computers than waste time cracking all your finicky traps, don't you think?
The man takes a step back hastily. His eyes dart between the three of you, calculating, weighing, assessing. Then, without a moment's hesitation, he turns and bolts.
You lunge to the side, cutting off his shortest escape route. Norma also moves quickly and with precision, stopping his retreat toward the other side.

The man tries to change direction, only to collide head-on with Eileen charging straight at him. She seizes his collar and wrenches him forward. You catch his wrist and twist it back, while Norma sweeps in with a kick, knocking him off balance cleanly.

Thud!
The man is slammed heavily to the ground, no longer able to resist.

When you leave the Public Security Bureau, you and Norma happen to be heading the same way. For the first time ever, she doesn't check her watch or turn down your suggestion to walk together for the sake of saving time. Instead, she's got something to tell you.

But once you actually start walking, she stays silent. You pass by one streetlight after another. Her fingers curl slightly, then relax. She seems to be running through every possible way to start the conversation in her mind, searching for the "best solution," yet unable to arrive at one.
You notice, but say nothing. You simply match her pace, unhurried, waiting for her to begin.
Finally...

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...Thank you!

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Huh?!
You're caught off guard by her sudden sentence. Norma reflexively pushes up her glasses, the tips of her ears flushing red as her gaze darts away, but she doesn't recoil.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I-I mean... Thank you for believing in me. For investigating this game with me, even when I didn't have enough evidence. And... for standing by my side through all of that.
Her voice trembles with nervousness, but she doesn't stop.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: And, and thank you for helping me clear Moses's name. That... meant a lot to me. I couldn't have done any of this without you.
You can't help but smile.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Who says you don't know how to express your feelings? You're killing it!

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Ugh! I-I... I'm not...
She fumbles, words catching in her throat, nothing like that sharp-tongued analyst during that debate.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Alright. I'll stop teasing you.
You clear your throat and put on a more serious tone.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I chose to trust you because you were persistent. Your abilities and your judgment were the reason why we were able to solve this case.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I might not have trusted a cold, purely numerical "model" so easily. But when you told me your story, I saw the "human" side of you.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I think both Eileen and that criminal were wrong about you. You are someone with feelings. You have a tireless passion for your work, and you care about everyone's safety. You may not be good at expressing emotions, but you do care. That's what helped me understand you. That's what made me trust you.

Norma doesn't respond right away. She ponders silently, as if breaking down your words, reorganizing them, then slowly integrating them into her understanding. After a long moment, she finally begins quietly.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...Perhaps you're right. Human emotions aren't completely pointless. In certain extreme situations, they can indeed produce... outcomes that exceed what any model could predict.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: That's right. Emotions are hard to quantify and accurately incorporate into models... but they're always there. Whether you try to analyze them or not, they'll always...
You pause for a moment.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Remind you that you actually care about certain people and certain things.
Norma seems dazed for a moment. She doesn't deny it. Instead, she lets out a soft breath, and a faint, somewhat bitter smile touches her lips.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Perhaps you're right.
After a brief silence, you change the subject.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Speaking of which... what are you planning to do about Eileen? You both clearly care about each other. It'd be a shame to just leave things like this, don't you think? Why not sit down and talk it through properly?
Norma's steps falter slightly. Her gaze drifts ahead, settling on nothing in particular.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: ...There's no need. I did hurt her back then. She was right. I shouldn't have imposed my logic on her. Maybe she would've been better off without me. Then she wouldn't have been so seriously traumatized. I have no right to ask for her forgiveness.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Just being able to see her again... was already a bonus. And besides...
Her voice softens slightly.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Eileen seems... better now than she was before. She was able to move on and recover. I'm glad for her.
You don't press further, only offering a soft hum of acknowledgment. As the sky turns dark, streetlights cast long shadows on the ground.
Another weekend arrives. You invite Eileen out and bring her all the way to Norma's apartment building.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: What exactly is this "fun activity" you're talking about?

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Following Norma.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Huh?! Hey, just because we had a falling out doesn't mean I'm going to help you stalk her!

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Shh. Follow me.
The building door clicks open. Norma steps out, her stride as brisk as ever.
You raise your hand, signaling Eileen to follow. She stamps her feet in protest but ultimately relents and catches up.
You tail her through the streets and watch as she enters a bank. Through the glass window, the counter's light falls on Norma, illuminating her calm and focused expression.

steps.speaker: Bank Teller
steps.content: Hi, Miss Norma, good to see you again. Same as usual? Fifteen transfers to the designated accounts? Would you like me to give you an update on their financial situations?

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: I've already reviewed the monthly reports. Johnny's family still lacks a sustainable income source. I'll set up an online game design course tailored to his situation next month. When he comes to withdraw his cash, please try to suggest to him that he could maybe become a game designer.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Also, please pay Holly's counseling fees while you're at it.
Eileen seems surprised.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Johnny and Holly... Could they be...
You nod, confirming her guess.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: That's right. Those are the victims from that incident years ago, or their family members.
Eileen doesn't say another word, simply watching Norma. Something shifts in her gaze.

steps.speaker: Bank Teller
steps.content: Don't worry, I'll take care of it. Miss Norma, you've been anonymously helping these families for years now. You truly have a heart of gold.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Don't call me Norma. How many times do I have to tell you? I go by Cindy here.

steps.speaker: Bank Teller
steps.content: Of course, Miss Norma.
The two are clearly well acquainted. Norma shoots the teller a sharp glare, but the teller only smiles, unfazed.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: ...You brought me here so I'd see the kindness Norma never displays in front of anyone, didn't you?
Eileen lowers her gaze and sighs softly.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: At first, when the pain was at its worst... I did resent her. I hated that she couldn't just be normal for once and understand how powerless I felt back then.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: But of course I knew she only wanted to help. It's just... in that state, I couldn't meet her expectations anymore. I was terrified of disappointing her, and I hated myself for not being able to just... heal faster.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: All of it piled up, bit by bit, until it crushed me. I projected the disgust I felt for myself on Norma... But maybe, deep down, I just wanted to push her away. So my pain wouldn't affect her anymore.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Maybe what hurt her was never being affected by your pain, but that you pushed her away. You might be one of the few friends she had... perhaps her only friend. So, will you consider giving her another chance?

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: Didn't I already give her a chance? But she actually locked me behind a fire door! Damn it, she still thought she was helping me...
Eileen's eyebrows shoot up, the edge returning to her voice. But she catches herself in the middle and stops. Her shoulders sag slightly as she shakes her head in resignation.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: ...Whatever. That's just how she is. Dumb and stubborn, always deciding things for others. Guess I'll just have to be more forgiving.
She lowers her head with a smile, her voice softening.

steps.speaker: Eileen
steps.content: I'll reach out to her again. She's an important friend to me. Always has been, and still is. All those memories we shared... I don't want to just let them go.
You look over at Norma.

A faint smile graces her face. She's likely already aware of those eyes on her back, yet she doesn't acknowledge it. Instead, she pretends not to notice, quietly watching some children play in the courtyard outside while continuing to fill out remittance forms at the counter.
As her pen glides over the paper, bright light filters in.
Golden sunlight falls upon her shoulders, just as it once did on the swing on that dorm balcony, all those years ago.
